articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi

The arrests came shortly after the League held its first National Congress, marking the organization’s formal effort to establish itself as a political organization representing working-class interests in Uganda. articles.title: Unabated violence: 47 dead and 60 kidnapped in Haiti in August 24 massacre
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: The violence in Haiti shows no signs of stopping. On August 24, 47 people were massacred in Kenscoff, near the capital, Port-au-Prince, according to the UN. Of the 47 people killed, 22 were murdered in a local church. According to authorities, the massacre took place amid a gang war for control of territories in the Caribbean nation. María Fernanda Arocha, an analyst with Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), told El País : “The latest attack in Kenscoff is yet another example of how gangs resort to large-scale killings of civilians to subdue the local population and impose their authority. articles.title: U.S. Empire in Decline: Richard Wolff on Iran War, Rising Inequality, $40T National Debt & More
articles.content_excerpt: We speak to Richard Wolff, a prominent Marxist economist, about the economic fallout from the war on Iran, which recently reached the six-month mark. “Because it’s only been going on for a few months, the impact on the prices we pay is about to unload itself,” says Wolff. The U.S. national debt, which recently topped $40 trillion, is “one of the many signs of an economy and of an empire that is now in decline,” says Wolff. “There is an enormous increase in defense spending, or now war spending, that is scheduled, and no comparable increase in revenue.” Wolff also discusses how a global selloff of U.S. government bonds means increasing borrowing costs for everyday consumers.

articles.title: “Went to Sea and Never Came Back”: Families of Fishermen Seek Answers After Deadly U.S. Boat Strikes
articles.content_excerpt: A year ago today, the United States bombed a small boat in the Caribbean, killing nine people on board. Two survivors clung to the wreckage for 45 minutes, reportedly waving for help, before a second “double-tap” strike killed them, too. President Trump posted a video of the first attack on social media, announcing that 11 terrorists had been killed in a military operation that would be called “Operation Southern Spear.” The second video, showing the killing of the survivors, has never been released. The bombings have continued for a year, killing at least 227 people in nearly 70 separate strikes. The Pentagon often accuses the boats it targets of narcotrafficking.
